newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Dec 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Dec 10.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Philippine Supreme Court clears the way for businessman Eduardo Cojuangco Jr to renew his bid to regain control of San Miguel Corp by ruling that an anti-graft court can entertain Cojuangco's petition to oust seven government nominees at the San Miguel Corp board (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- A group of congressmen opposing moves to amend the Philippine Constitution challenges President Fidel Ramos to sign a manifesto opposing such changes to prove that he is not behind the new initiative to extend his term beyond 1998 (TODAY/PHILIPPINE STAR/CHRONICLE)
- The administration party, LAKAS-NUCD, is behind the signature campaign seeking to amend the Constitution and expand the term of President Ramos (MANILA TIMES)
- The influential Catholic Bishops' Conference of the Philippines and leftist groups vow to oppose any changes in the Constitution that would extend the term of the President (INQUIRER)
- Korea Electric Power Corp emerges as the lowest bidder for the 1,200-megawatt gas-fired power plant of the National Power Corp (BULLETIN/PHILIPPINE STAR/MANILA TIMES/ BUSINESSWORLD/STANDARD)

- The Philippines wants the World Trade Organisation (WTO) to seriously pursue trade liberalisation and junk non-tariff trade barriers particularly in the areas of textile and agriculture, Trade Minister Cesar Bautista said in a speech before the WTO Ministerial Conference (INQUIRER)
- The Philippine government expresses before the WTO its concern about other members' noncompliance with agreements set forth in the Uruguay Round global trade accord (MANILA TIMES/BUSINESSWORLD)

- President Fidel Ramos says the long-delayed bidding for the privatisation of state-run television station Intercontinental Broadcasting Corp (IBC) or Channel 13 will push through on December 27 despite alleged irregularities in the bidding procedure (PHILIPPINE STAR)
